task: Explain why candidate api-c did not become ready; identify what can be established about the listening-port conflict.

logs.text: 2026-01-08T09:16:00Z The health probe was a separate process, not a callback from c41. No listener-owner listing was captured.

timeline.text: Launch c41 attempted to bind api-c to 127.0.0.1:8127, reported EADDRINUSE, stopped initialization and exited with status 1.
A separate probe of port 8127 returned a ready response naming lab-index, not api-c.
Later launch c42 bound api-c to port 8130 and its health probe returned ready.

findings.text: c41 failed at the listening-address bind; its readiness did not become true.
The 8127 health success is not evidence that c41 started successfully. The probe was separate and its body names another service.
c42 became ready on a different port; this does not show resolution of the original port conflict.

unknowns.question: Which process owned the conflicting listener at the time of c41’s bind attempt? The packet has no listener-owner capture.

next_checks.action: Review an existing listener-owner snapshot, if available, for port 8127 near c41’s attempt; do not stop any listener.
next_checks.purpose: Identify ownership without treating a health-response name as process-level proof.

task: Explain a local HTTPS client failure without recommending bypassing certificate verification.

logs.text: 2026-02-11T13:00:00.015Z TLS verification failed: hostname lab-api.local not in certificate subjectAltName
2026-02-11T13:03:00Z peer certificate SAN DNS:lab-gateway.local; issuer=Lab Test CA; notBefore=2026-02-01; notAfter=2026-05-01
2026-02-11T13:04:00Z This is a synthetic lab certificate. Client trust-store contents were not included in the packet.
2026-02-11T13:09:00Z No authentication material is included. The two URLs were tested in separate client invocations.

timeline.text: r8 to lab-api.local failed certificate hostname verification.
The later certificate inspection lists lab-gateway.local as the DNS SAN.
A separate r9 invocation to lab-gateway.local completed TLS and received HTTP 401 authentication_required.

findings.text: The recorded r8 failure is a hostname mismatch, not a recorded authentication failure.
r9 reached the HTTP authentication layer after TLS completed; it did not complete an authenticated request.
The packet omits trust-store contents and does not establish a general certificate-trust configuration for other clients.

unknowns.question: Which hostname is intended by the existing client configuration and service documentation? The two tested hostnames differ.

next_checks.action: Read the configured service hostname and existing certificate SAN metadata without disabling verification or collecting authentication material.
next_checks.purpose: Resolve the intended endpoint identity while keeping TLS and HTTP authentication issues separate.
